## Source pin — read 2026-10-13T00:30:53Z

Everything marked `[VERIFIED]` was read on **13 Oct 2026** through the n8n gateway
**`[GATEWAY] HubSpot Read`**, workflow `fCFvIDxxSi2F4re3`:

- gateway `versionId` **`b9418bd0-c3c4-4d73-9b62-c4bc21487b83`**, `updatedAt` **2026-10-12T01:56:22.045Z**, active: true
- `GET /automation/v4/flows` → **816 flows** (510 enabled)
- `GET /automation/v4/flows/{id}` → **816 full definitions, 0 errors**
- **sha256 of the canonical flow set: `437b09c6eb031ddc85157520dbd86d9b2a5bd67a8fdbeca2119ba359ec54d264`**

That last line is the staleness test. A HubSpot flow has a `revisionId`, but the portal has no
single version number, so the pin is a hash over every flow's `(id, name, isEnabled, revisionId,
updatedAt)`. **If a later run computes a different sha, the portal moved and this diagram is
stale.**

A description of a hash is not a reproducible test, so here is the exact canonical form:

```python
rows = sorted((str(f["id"]), f.get("name") or "", bool(f.get("isEnabled")),
               str(f.get("revisionId")), str(f.get("updatedAt")))
              for f in GET("/automation/v4/flows"))
sha256(json.dumps(rows, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
```

`verify_pin.py` (attached to PRO-46, beside `gw.py`) runs exactly this and exits 0 for FRESH,
1 for STALE. It needs only the gateway token and makes one read-only list call.

## Conventions — PRO-36's, and README rule 3

**Provenance is the border and the bracket tag, never colour.** Colour already carries meaning in
the operator's own map; overloading it would destroy both signals.

- solid green, thick — `[VERIFIED]` read from live HubSpot config (date on the page-00 legend)
- dashed amber — `[CACHE 1 Sep 2026]` from the stale extract
- dotted purple — `[OPERATOR]` an operator claim, not machine-checked
- dashed red, thick — `[BLIND SPOT]` a known gap

**Fill carries state** (white ON / grey OFF / pale red dead end / lilac asset / blue n8n) and
**the lane is the page**. At 816 boxes, ON-vs-OFF has to read at a glance.

## The four requirements

1. **Links.** 1,509 boxes carry an mxGraph `link=`: **1,406 flow links** (816 distinct flows,
   some drawn on more than one page), **45 property links**, **18 list links** and **40 internal
   page jumps**. The **flow** URL format is VERIFIED (taken from a URL the portal itself
   generated). **The property and list formats are INFERRED and have never been clicked** —
   nobody here has a browser. One click each settles them, and they live in single functions of
   the generator. **Forms are drawn but are not clickable:** no form URL appears anywhere in the
   file, so listing forms among the inferred link formats — as an earlier draft of this note did
   — was wrong.
2. **Dead ends — page 15.** Now including the half stage 1 could not deliver:
   **397 empty branch arms across 85 flows (46 enabled)**. A branch that names a cohort,
   matches it, and connects to nothing. Stage 1 had no branch tree and said so; the live
   definition carries one. Also 6 enabled flows with zero actions.
3. **Deactivated, drawn in place — page 16.** 306 OFF flows, each on the page it would have run
   on, grey, still carrying its triggers. **251 of the 306 still have an automatic trigger** —
   a form, list, property or event criterion that would fire the moment the switch is flipped.
   The other 55 are MANUAL-only and would need someone to enrol records by hand.
4. **Assets, not just workflows — pages 3, 4, 18, 19.** Deal pipelines and stages, the trigger
   layer (forms, landing pages, lists, unified events, email events, integration events, ads),
   properties, lists with their live reference counts, and the webhook / custom-code / SMS actions
   that reach outside HubSpot.

## What stage 2 changed that matters

- **Every trigger is resolved.** The cache saw only property and list criteria, so 201 of 767 flows
  showed no trigger and no *"nothing triggers X"* claim was safe. Live definitions resolve the
  trigger for **all 510 enabled flows — zero unknowns**. Forms, landing pages, unified events,
  email events, integration events and one ads trigger were all invisible before.
- **The contact lifecycle has 9 stages, not 7.** `Game Plan Booked` (`1168996898`) is a **custom**
  stage inside the standard pipeline. PRO-37 said five, stage 1 corrected it to seven, and both
  were wrong. Page 2.
- **Flow → flow enrolment is real control flow.** 125 `0-15` edges across 122 flows; every target
  resolves. Deactivating a source silently starves everything below it. Page 14.
- **`dealstage` is the most contended property**: 23 writers (20 enabled), ahead of
  `hs_lead_status` at 20. 77 properties have more than one writer. Page 17.
- **Drift since 1 Sep**: 49 flows new, 0 deleted, 9 flipped ON/OFF, 20 edited. One flow went from
  147 to 382 actions. Page 20.

## What the conversion could NOT carry

README rule 5 — these are recorded as named gaps on **page 21**, not quietly dropped.

| Gap | Why |
|---|---|
| Ticket, company, product, quote, subscription, line-item and appointment **properties** | HubSpot returns **403** — the gateway credential lacks the scope |
| **Object schemas** | `/crm/v3/schemas` returns 0 results, so custom objects (`2-49225926`, `2-21217427`, `2-49225923`, `2-49225924`, `2-56668494`, `2-64252538`) are named by id only |
| Reads by **numeric `objectTypeId`** | the gateway allowlist's object segment is `[A-Za-z0-9_]+` — **no hyphen** — so `/crm/v3/properties/0-1` is refused and only name forms work. Custom objects have no name form. AutomationEngineer's change; I am read-only |
| **Marketing email bodies** | 246 flows send email by `content_id`; bodies and any URL inside them were never fetched |
| **Installed apps / integrations list** | not in the gateway allowlist, so dialer.io, Kixie, Zapier and Dialfire remain inferred from flow names and webhook URLs |
| **Sequences, CTAs, ads objects** | separate objects that move contacts, absent from the flow API. One flow *is* triggered by an ads interaction, which proves ads reach into the estate |
| **Operator-note preservation** | the generator emits an **empty** `operator-notes` layer every run. Layer separation is necessary and **not sufficient** — the merge step does not exist |

## Regenerating

```
export N8N_GATEWAY_TOKEN=...   # HubSpot, through the gateway
export N8N_API_KEY=...         # only for the 1 Sep drift baseline table
python3 fetch.py               # every live read -> flows_live.json, defs/, lists, forms, pin, drift
python3 analyze.py             # defs/*.json -> analysis.json
python3 build_map_stage2.py    # -> hubspot-logic-map.drawio
python3 verify_map.py          # mechanical checks; exits non-zero on a structural fault
```

`fetch.py`, `analyze.py`, `build_map_stage2.py`, `verify_map.py`, `verify_pin.py` and `gw.py` are
attached to Paperclip task **PRO-46**.

**`fetch.py` is new on 13 Oct and closes a real gap.** The stage-2 artifact set shipped the
*builder* but not the *fetcher*, so "the rebuild is one command" was only true for a run that
still had the intermediate JSON on disk. It is true for anyone now. `fetch.py` was validated by
rebuilding the 12 Oct file from scratch and accounting for every line of difference.

The raw reads are not committed here because they contain contact-shaped data; the diagram names
systems, flows, lists and properties — **not people** (README rule 6).

One caveat on that rule: a handful of flows are *named* after a person by whoever created them
(for example `Test - Renewal Workflow - sara`). That is the flow's own name in HubSpot config, not
a contact record, and it is reproduced verbatim because renaming it here would make the map stop
matching the portal.
